#sqlite #databases

My side project and the local fake of our KYC vendor both run on SQLite. Settings that stuck: `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL; PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000;`. Before WAL, the load test with 8 concurrent writer tasks got "database is locked" on about 3% of requests. After: zero, and readers no longer block the writer. Gotcha one: the `-wal` file grew to 1.9 GB because a long-lived read connection kept checkpoints from finishing. `wal_autocheckpoint` defaults to 1000 pages; I added a `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` every 10 minutes. Gotcha two: WAL doesn't work over NFS. Don't try. I tried, November 2023, on the Synology DS220+, and lost an evening. Gotcha three: copying the `.db` file without its `-wal` and `-shm` siblings gives you a backup that looks corrupted; use `.backup` or `VACUUM INTO 'snap.db'` instead. Proper backups for the real databases are in [[Backup and point-in-time restore]]. Pool size for SQLite is 1 writer, many readers, unlike [[Connection pooling]] for Postgres.
